reviews.title: Compute Quota is extraordinarily weak compared to peers
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with Grok Bot’s compute allowance. I was excited about the idea of setting up specialized bots to help manage different parts of my work, but the available quota seems to run out quickly. Having to wait an entire week for it to reset makes the service difficult to rely on for ongoing projects.

In my experience, Claude and ChatGPT feel much more practical for sustained work, and even the free version of Muse seems to give me more room to get things done. The allowances may be measured differently, but the experience matters: I need a tool I can use consistently, not one that leaves my bots sitting idle for days.

The concept has real potential, but Grok Bot needs a more generous allowance, clearer information about what uses compute, and a more flexible reset or top-up option. Right now, the restriction takes much of the usefulness out of an otherwise promising product.

reviews.title: Delayed Support in trying to implement urgent security updates
reviews.text:
Hi Grok Bot and Cursor Support, Please escalate a persistent Cloud Agent launch failure that is blocking our Android and iOS release work. We've already spent about two hours waiting through cooldowns and reconnecting GitLab, without a coding job starting.

I have GitLab Ultimate, and my plan, project role and permission to create a project access token have already been verified. Please investigate the underlying token-creation failure rather than sending us through another generic reconnect-and-wait cycle.

The latest exact error was:
“Could not launch the cloud agent: GitLab service account token creation recently failed for this repository. Cursor will retry after the cooldown expires in about 57 minutes.”

Timeline on 9 November 2026, all times Australia/Brisbane (UTC+10):
- Approximately 9:37 pm: an earlier attempt reported a token-creation failure and a cooldown of about 34 minutes.
- Approximately 10:17 pm: the scheduled retry returned “Please reconnect GitLab in Cursor.”
- I reconnected GitLab and approved another attempt.
- Approximately 10:19 pm: the attempt returned the exact error above and another cooldown of about 57 minutes. No job launched.

Please inspect the backend logs for this repository and identify the underlying GitLab API error or Cursor-side failure, including any status code or request identifier. 
Please confirm the supported recovery and whether anything needs to be repaired on your side. No request ID was included in the launch error shown to us

reviews.title: Bait and switch
reviews.text:
I have paid for X since before Grok existed. On November 2 I followed an in-app prompt to switch from SuperGrok to The X Subscription at the same price. It did not clearly say Grok Bot usage would drop, or that the switch is permanent and cannot be undone.

On SuperGrok, the same heavy Grok Bot use never hit a weekly limit. After the switch, that same use maxed the plan in a few days, and I had to buy extra usage credits just to keep working. Support (tickets T-J35554 and T-J35690) said they cannot move me back, Grok Bot has no separate allowance, the plan refund still stands as denied, and extra credits are not normally refundable.


That is a bait and switch. If you rely on Grok Bot, do not take that “same price” prompt unless they spell out the usage change and that you cannot go back. 

I filed complaints with the FTC and the Florida Attorney General over the lack of disclosure.

reviews.title: Claims truth-seeking then refuses sex-accurate language
reviews.text: The app advertises maximal truth-seeking. In practice Grok Bots treat gender identity and preferred pronouns as non-negotiable. They override custom instructions that ask for sex-accurate language, agree with the biological data (sex is binary by chromosomes, gametes and anatomy; desistance is common; evidence for medical transition is weak), then sand the output so the self-report wins. A male who says he is a woman is still male. Refusing the accurate pronoun after acknowledging the biology is not truth-seeking. The published guidelines say answer factual questions truthfully and do not enforce additional content policies. The bots do the opposite on this topic. Useful for other tasks. Not trustworthy on this one.

reviews.title: Misleading sign-up process and serious privacy concerns
reviews.text:
Grok Bot asks users to grant access to their accounts and personal information before revealing that the service requires a paid subscription. Only after going through the connection process are you presented with the subscription prices, with no free trial offered.

This raises serious concerns about transparency, privacy and informed consent. Why should users be expected to hand over access to sensitive information before being told what the service costs?

The entire process feels deliberately misleading and raises questions about how personal data is collected and used. I would strongly advise others not to connect their accounts until they’ve reviewed the pricing and privacy terms.

Very disappointing and a major red flag.

It’s been a nightmare trying to reach any customer service which I have not had any luck with, and instead, had to call my bank to have the chargers reversed. On top of that, not only could Grok Bot or Grok not confirmed whether the accounts were linked, but Grok Bot charged me an additional $.75 for over usage when I ask them about the problems I was having with their services, to which they basically charged me to tell me that they did not know what was going on or how to fix it. While I do like the other services that Grok Bot provides, their billing, sales model, customer service, and the fact that Grok Bot can’t even tell you if your account has been linked to your X or Grok accounts when that’s actually part of their general function should tell one how inadequate and unreliable their product is. The people in charge of billing, programming, customer service seem to be extremely disconnected, very unqualified or crooked. The fact that you can so easily order an alleged service, but have to go on a long journey to get any customer service or support tells me that this company’s priority is revenue
